messages:
Zoe (Strategy): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A. Teams want concrete guidance on: 1) where to allocate hiring and engineering effort across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, 2) a tight sales qualification checklist for when to propose Dedicated, 3) how to frame our differentiation vs cloud bundles and self-hosted runtimes in one sentence.

Jordan (CEO): Short take: keep mission steady  make inference reliable, fast, and cost-predictable for builders. Hiring tilt this year: 55% infra & runtime (to scale Hosted), 25% Dedicated product/infra (SLA + enterprise features), 20% Private/compliance & partner integrations. We need to keep runway across tracks but scale Hosted faster for PLG motion.

Kemi (Eng): For planning: do we freeze new Dedicated UX experiments? We need clarity for sprint allocation.

Jordan (CEO): No freeze. Dedicated UX/enterprise features continue, but big new experiments should be deprioritized unless they unlock >$X ARR or are security-critical. Keep Dedicated reliability and rollout tooling fully staffed.

Mateo (Product): Sales qualification checklist request: proposal to use a simple 4-point scorecard: 1) sustained spend (placeholder $30k/mo), 2) peak QPS above shared pool headroom, 3) compliance/data residency needs, 4) workload type (embedding-heavy or low-latency streams). If score >=2, flag for Dedicated outreach. Thoughts?

Priya (Sales): Love the scorecard. Can we add "team readiness" (has SRE/infra or not) as a negative signal for self-hosting?

Jordan (CEO): Add that. Finalize with RevOps; use it in the playbook as a checklist for SDRs/AMs.

Kemi (Eng): Competitive framing: we should call out three engineering differentiators: 1) unified runtime (same behavior across modes), 2) predictable unit economics (batching, cache, quantization choices surfaced), 3) graceful degradation (automatic fallback to compatible variants). One-sentence public line: "Redwood gives teams a single inference runtime across hosted, reserved, and private environments so they get predictable latency and transparent cost controls without rebuilding ops."

Mateo (Product): Add a short internal variant for decks: "Production inference without the ops lift." Keep public copy slightly more descriptive.

Priya (Sales): Also need an objection-handling snippet: prospect: "cloud vendor X has discounts and model access." Reply: "For experiments, great. For production, you want predictable SLOs, clear cost levers, and a vendor-agnostic model catalog with rollback/fallback policies  that's where Redwood helps."

Zoe (Strategy): Can leadership confirm whether we want to share any quantitative claims (e.g., % cost reduction)? Marketing asks for guardrails.

Jordan (CEO): Use conservative phrasing: "Customers often see improved cost and latency through our batching, caching, and model optimization guidance; ask for a workload-specific benchmark." Reserve percent claims for vetted case studies.

Mateo (Product): Action items: I'll update the roadmap hiring plan to match the 55/25/20 split and add the Dedicated flag gating for major experiments. Kemi, please draft the engineering differentiators doc and compatibility policy for runtime changes. Priya, add the scorecard and objection scripts to the playbook and mark thresholds as provisional. Zoe, put the messaging lines into the strategy packet.

Kemi (Eng): I'll draft SLO targets we can propose (p50/p95 latency bands, cost/token goals, cold-start thresholds) and include requirements for opt-in runtime flags for Dedicated/Private.

Priya (Sales): I'll roll the scorecard into the playbook today and ping RevOps for final thresholds.

RecorderBot: Recording and notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/recordings/2365556789  deck and playbook drafts in the shared drive.

Jordan (CEO): Thanks team. If anyone else has follow-ups, drop them here or DM Zoe.
